newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy PM asks govt to reject Di Pietro resignation.
newsitem.headline: Italy PM asks govt to reject Di Pietro resignation.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday he would ask his government to reject Antonio Di Pietro's resignation as public works minister.
Earlier, former graft-busting magistrate Di Pietro said in a letter to Prodi he was resigning from the government after himself coming under investigation in a corruption probe.

"I will ask the government to reject the resignation. I hope that Di Pietro will go back on his decision and continue to give his precious contribution to the government's work," Prodi told parliament.

Di Pietro wrote in his letter that his decision was irreversible and said he had become the victim of a "pigeon shoot". The shock resignation followed confirmation that he was the subject of a preliminary investigation by magistrates in the northern town of Brescia.

Newspapers on Thursday said Di Pietro was being probed over alleged irregularities in the way he conducted his inquiries while a member of the elite pool of "Clean Hands" magistrates in Milan that exposed deep corruption in politics.
He entered politics in May when Prodi asked him to join his newly formed centre-left government.
